Figure 2.2 Some examples of unintentional mechanisms

Buckling is the loss of stability due to geometric nonlinearity arising from the
deflection of part or whole of the structure. Unlike bodily movement, buckling
causes straining of the structure and is thus dependent on the stiffness of the
structural elements involved (mainly the lateral stiffness of struts and out-of-
plane stiffness of walls). It is basically a second order effect (also referred to as
